sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Onboarding flows for visitors and new accounts
sections.what: Steps a visitor through three onboarding screens by keyboard and checks the saved language and sports cookies, then registers an account and checks the saved preferences on that account.
sections.why: Confirms first-run choices are kept for both guests and signed-in users.
sections.watch_out: The expected cookie values and default selections are fixed, so changing defaults requires updating these tests.

summary: Browser tests of the three-step onboarding for new visitors and for newly registered accounts, checking keyboard navigation, saved sports and language, and that choices are stored on the account.
purpose: Confirms the first-run setup works by keyboard and that the sports and language choices are kept.
why: Onboarding decides what a user sees first, so it must work without a mouse and save choices correctly.
how: The first test opens onboarding, steps through three screens checking titles, step labels, pictogram count and accessibility, moving forward with the keyboard. It picks Football and Hindi, starts, and checks the language and sports cookies are set. The second test registers a new account, signs in, goes to onboarding, picks Tennis, starts, and checks the saved preferences show cricket and tennis with English.
inputs: The onboarding pages, the new user account and the cookies.
outputs: Pass or fail for navigation, accessibility, cookies and saved preferences.
risks: The tests expect default sports and language values, and the account test expects cricket to be preselected, so changing defaults breaks them.
debug: If a cookie check fails, inspect the cookies in the browser after finishing onboarding. If the saved preferences differ, check the preferences endpoint.
